text:
The evidence can't tell us whether storm damage caused the 2023 loss. It shows that loss happened but says nothing about why.

What it shows: Hansen/UMD mapped about 4.5 ha of tree-cover loss in 2023 within ASSET-A, roughly 0.12% of the 3,643.5 ha property. Later years through 2025 were observed, and the JRC 2020 forest reference agrees across the whole event area. The MGAP 2021 map classes about 4.3 ha as planted forest (Pinus elliottii and Pinus taeda), with 0.2 ha outside mapped forest and no native forest. A further 1.3 ha of loss in patches under 0.5 ha was not counted as an event.

What it doesn't show: Hansen loss records any stand replacement, so harvest, fire, storm, or clearing look the same. The data also can't establish legality, responsibility, or compliance.

To answer your question, you would need other evidence, such as harvest records, storm event reports, or fire data for 2023.
